$comment: Eval-rig manifest. Drives apps/api/scripts/eval-parse.ts. Hand-authored fixtures with explicit variety on domain, voice, detail level, and information gaps. AI-authored on 2026-05-15 — replace with human-written docs at any point.

fixtures.scenario: Detailed founder-voice brief from a small powerlifting/strongman gym. Lowercase, casual, lots of specifics (member count, sponsored athletes, equipment list).
fixtures.notable: Domain is clear. Tests USP extraction (specific equipment counts, sponsorships), pricePoint inference from sparse signals, brandPersonality from casual founder voice.

fixtures.scenario: Agency-prepared formal brief for a pediatric dental practice. Numbered sections, third-person voice, complete information.
fixtures.notable: Clean baseline. Should not be hard for the parser. Tests: domainSpecifier extraction, pricePoint=mid (explicitly stated), specific targetAudience.

fixtures.scenario: Two-sentence founder note. Just enough to identify the business. Missing most optional fields.
fixtures.notable: Sparse. Missing fields: tagline, contact email, phone, USPs, brandPersonality cues are minimal. Tests parser's ability to NOT invent missing data.

fixtures.scenario: Bulleted fill-in-the-blank style brief — has the structure of a marketing template. Explicit pricePoint, explicit USPs, explicit brand vibes.
fixtures.notable: All fields well-supplied. Tests verbatim USP extraction. brandPersonality should match the listed 'vibes' (quiet, unfussy, old-money-ish).

fixtures.scenario: Long, formal brief for a UK technology consultancy. Very B2B. Detailed practice areas.
fixtures.expectedDomainSpecifierHint: cloud architecture and platform engineering consultancy
fixtures.notable: Tricky: could land in `it_services` or `consulting`. Either is defensible. Tests: long-document handling, pricePoint=premium (explicit), restrained voice extraction.

fixtures.scenario: Founder voice. Boutique fitness + wellness + cafe hybrid. The founder explicitly notes the category is hard to pin down.
fixtures.expectedDomainSpecifierHint: boutique fitness/wellness hybrid with IV therapy and cafe
fixtures.notable: DELIBERATELY AMBIGUOUS. Defensible answers: yoga_wellness, salon_spa, gym_fitness, other. Consistency matters more than the specific call. domainSpecifier should carry the nuance.

fixtures.scenario: Boutique Toronto immigration practice. Self-describes as 'closer to consulting than lawyering' but is licensed as a law firm.
fixtures.notable: DELIBERATELY AMBIGUOUS. law_firm or consulting are both defensible. The fact that they are licensed as a law firm should anchor to law_firm in my read, but the parser may disagree.

fixtures.scenario: One-paragraph minimum-viable brief for an SAT/ACT tutoring service. Almost no information beyond domain + name.
fixtures.notable: EXTREMELY sparse. Missing: location, contact, audience specifics, USPs, brandPersonality cues, pricePoint signal. Strongest test of 'don't invent' rule.

fixtures.scenario: Founder phone-typed message. Specific, casual, full of business detail. Buyer-only real estate agency.
fixtures.notable: Tests USP extraction (the no-listings principle), targetAudience specificity (3 distinct buyer segments), pricePoint quirk (commission-based, no direct cost to buyer).

fixtures.scenario: Brief that mixes formal agency-prepared opening with founder-voice asides (including 'i wrote drunk at 1am' aside).
fixtures.notable: Tests brandPersonality extraction from a deliberately-stated voice profile ('dry, slightly arch'). USPs are stated as 'studio principles'. pricePoint=premium (explicit £45k starting fee).
